MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 26, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Pro Tem Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on January 26, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo,
California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 21, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury (arrived at 5:40 p.m.)

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

City Council Minutes  1  January 26, 2016
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The
City Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed a personnel review and there was
no disclosable action from Closed Session.

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Mission Viejo High School Varsity Football Team as the 2015 CIF- State
  Championship Division 1-AA Champions

  Mayor Ury and Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum presented certificates of commendation to the
  coaches and athletes of the Mission Viejo High School Varsity Football Team.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Rhonda Reardon, M.V.: discussed the life of Tom "Richie" Pearson, a WWII Veteran and Mission
Viejo resident who recently passed away.

Jacklyn Flowers, M.V.: thanked the City of Mission Viejo for issuing a proclamation for the
International Day of Happiness and invited the Council Members to a showcase for the day at the
Norman P. Murray Community Center on Saturday, March 12, 2016.

Penny Lambright, Huntington Beach: introduced an Orange County non-profit organization called
Patriots and Paws which provides active and reservist veterans with services and free rescue
animals.

David Anderson, Saddleback College, M.V.: thanked the City Council for the Community Grant
to support Summer of Theater for Saddleback College and the Angels of the Arts.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 5, 12, 13, and 14 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

City Council Minutes  2  January 26, 2016
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 12, 2016, as
  presented.

4.  Check Register Dated December 24, 2015 in the Amount of $1,155,245.67

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2015

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2015

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for November 2015

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  November 2015

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  January 26, 2016
 10.  Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the 16-17 A-B Annual Fiscal Period of
  July 1, 2016 to June 30, 2017

  Adopted Successor Agency Resolution No. 16-01 Approving the Recognized Obligation
  Payment Schedule for the 16-17 A-B for the Annual Fiscal Period of July 1, 2016, to June
  30, 2017, Including the FY 16-17 Administrative Budget, Subject to Submittal to, and
  Review by the Oversight Board and Then by the State Department of Finance Pursuant to
  California Health and Safety Code, Division 34, Part 1.85; Authorizing the Posting and
  Transmittal Thereof.

11.  Ordinances Regarding Operational Policies for Parks and Recreational Facilities

  (1) Adopted Ordinance 16-310 Amending Chapter 13.02.060 of Title 13 Relating to
  Operational Policies for Parks and Recreation Facilities (User Groups); and (2) adopted
  Ordinance 16-311 Amending Chapter 13.02.085 of Title 13 Relating to Operational
  Policies for Parks and Recreational Facilities (Additional items).

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated December 18, 2015 in the Amount of $563,989.70

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment made to Constance Phillips for
  succession planning and workforce analysis.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that one of the goals established last year was to begin
  succession planning given the number of retirees that the City is currently experiencing
  and expecting in the future. Ms. Phillips has also been asked to conduct an organizational
  study of the Library and Recreation departments as a result of the numerous changes in
  staffing in those two areas.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

5.  Check Register Dated January 8, 2016 in the Amount of $751,715.95

  Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment to Management Partners, Inc. for
  consulting services for Recreation and Community Services.
City Council Minutes  4  January 26, 2016
   City Manager Dennis Wilberg noted that it was assistance with the organizational study in
  the Recreation department that he mentioned under agenda item 3.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

12.  Pavion Park Restroom Construction - CIP 304

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that the City is rejecting an awful lot of bids
  and, as a result, contractors will not want to take the time and effort to bid in Mission Viejo.

  City Attorney Curley explained his recommendation to reject the bids and rebid the project.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to
  reject all bids and authorize staff to re-bid project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 1

  Council Member Schlicht expressed appreciation to Mayor Ury for bringing up the issue
  of the contractor's performance bond and she asked if that is what brought them back
  around to honoring the contract.

  Council Member Sachs expressed his opposition to rewarding the contractor for
  underestimating the project.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to table this matter for
  two weeks.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  January 26, 2016
   AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

14.  First Amendment to the Agreement with Ashbritt, Inc., for Disaster-Related Debris
  Management and Recovery Services

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she pulled this item from the Consent Calendar
  to stay consistent with her prior no vote.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the First
  Amendment to the agreement with Ashbritt, Inc., extending the term of the contract
  through May 22, 2016.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

15.  Marguerite Aquatics Complex Design Review

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in favor of the proposed design and thanked the City Council and staff
  for their time, support and effort in the process: Diving Coach T. Sorenson, M.V. and
  Nadadores Foundation Board Member and Dive Committee President, Kimberly Barnes,
  M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Raths, to
  approve the design development documentation and authorize staff to proceed ahead with
  working drawing preparation.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

16.  Revoke and replace the Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance (Ordinance 09-277)
  with updated Water Efficiency Ordinance
City Council Minutes  6  January 26, 2016
   Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to revoke Ordinance
  Number 09-277 "Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance," for administrative convenience,
  in its entirety and replace it with a similarly regulating Ordinance by introduction of
  Ordinance 16-312 Amending Chapter 8.12 of the Mission Viejo Municipal code entitled,
  "Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance."

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

17.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury presented the report.

18.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

19.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

20.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

City Council Minutes  7  January 26, 2016
 Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths congratulated Ron Ruef and Grant Voss who were selected as Community
Services Commission Chairman and Vice Chairman for 2016. He announced that he has been
hosting coffee events for residents at his home and he has heard many positive comments about
the outlook for the City. Residents are pleased with the balanced budget, the aquatics center
renovation, economic development and all of the activities that the City sponsors. Council
Member Raths said that the people he has talked to are excited about the economic development
efforts at the civic core and he thanked Mayor Ury for appointing him to the Economic
Development ad hoc committee so he can work hand in hand with Council Member Sachs and
City staff. He said that residents are also pleased with how well the apartments turned out on Oso
Parkway and are happy that Mayor Ury and Council Member Schlicht are getting along
better. Council Member Raths noted that some of the concerns he has heard from residents are the
single lane freeway on ramp at Oso Parkway, the sound fence along the eastern side of the I-5
freeway between Mission Viejo High School and the Country Club golf course, and the youth drug
abuse problem. He noted that his personal focus for 2016 will be continuing in economic
development and working with veterans throughout Orange County. He shared that he is a proud
member of the local Veteran of Foreign Wars and American Legion and he sits on Assembly
Member Bill Brough’s Veteran’s Advisory Committee and Supervisor Lisa Bartlett recently
appointed him to the Orange County Veterans Council. He also serves as President of the
Executive Board for Patriots and Paws which finds and trains rescue dogs and matches them with
veterans. Additionally, Patriots and Paws has a 7,000 square-foot facility full of furniture, beds,
dressers, refrigerators and other items that are given to veterans at no charge. Council Member
Raths concluded his comments by sharing a video on the special companionship of dogs.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs discussed his comments at the last meeting when he talked about the
impact that the new GASB (Governmental Accounting Standards Board) rules have on cities. He
stated that the impact was further brought to his attention when he was in Sacramento attending
League of City meetings. The majority of meetings that he attended dealt with problems at
CalPERS. One of the board members shared some information about the issues that the State faces
and cities may be facing and he said that it was quite enlightening. Council Member Sachs
discussed discount rates and return periods and expressed his concern for pensioners. He shared
that the CalPERS portfolio dropped 16% in the first 16 days of January and they pay $1.1 billion
in fees annually. The new Board Members are grappling with the things that need to be done. One
option is to reduce the amount of portfolio impact that require fee payments and another is to divest
of the volatile real estate holdings. Council Member Sachs stated that the key thing to understand
is the current market volatility and the geopolitical volatility throughout the world affect markets
and pensions. He noted that he is looking forward to his meeting with staff later in the week to
talk about income verses payments in the City’s budget. He has also shared that he has changed
his mind and he now thinks the City should pay its pension liability to 100% as quickly as possible.

City Council Minutes  8  January 26, 2016
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht and the Council observed a moment of silence for her dad, who recently
passed away.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum agreed that Patriots and Paws is an organization that does great things
and she encouraged Council Member Raths to keep up the good work. She also offered her
assistance with any local Patriots and Paws events. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum outlined her
attendance at the Building Industry Association meeting where Dr. Esmael Adibi of Chapman
University discussed the situation in China and its worldwide impact on housing and CalPERS
pensions, among other things. She announced that the 2nd annual Economic Coalition Report will
be held at Saddleback College on February 2 and she encouraged the Council members to attend.
She also invited residents to “Walk with Wendy” on February 13 beginning at the back door of
the community center at 8:00 a.m. The group will walk on the Oso Creek Trail and conduct a sort
of outdoor town hall meeting. She said that residents can learn about things that are going on and
ask questions, and everyone is welcome. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum announced that she wrote an
article for the Mission Viejo Reporter newspaper about protecting oneself and how people can
help in their own communities and neighborhoods. She also announced that Lisa Dunn, a Mission
Viejo resident, is holding a program for veterans on the topic of purchasing a home. It will be held
on Saturday, January 30, from 1:30-2:00 p.m. at the Orange County Fairgrounds and additional
information can be found at www.ochomefair.com. In conclusion, Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
shared a quote from Dr. Esmael Adibi: “The greatest reward in life is changing the life of another.”

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury told Council Member Sachs that that he would like to speak to him about paying the
pension liability to 100%. He said that he feels differently about making long term strategic
decisions based on 20 days of market performance and they can talk further about that and the
budget. He announced that he and his wife joined the Elks last night and he is looking forward to
participating and giving back to the community through the Elks. In conclusion, Mayor Ury stated
that there is a very special bond between a father and a daughter, and he expressed his condolences
to Council Member Schlicht on the loss of her dad.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:53 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Douglas Conrad Schlicht and Tom "Richie"
Pearson, to Tuesday, February, 9, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 9, 2016
City Council Minutes  9  January 26, 2016
